title: A resolution expressing the sense of the Senate regarding the importance of religious freedom, authoritative texts, and transparency in artificial intelligence systems.
action: Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S4958; text: CR S4951)
summary: The Senate stresses that artificial intelligence should respect religious freedom and incorporate authoritative texts as guiding principles. The resolution also calls for greater transparency in AI systems to promote accountability and public trust.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: This policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security, through the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to create a pilot program that uses artificial intelligence to defend critical infrastructure from cyber threats. The program aims to test and develop AI-based cyber‑defense strategies and tools, laying the groundwork for broader deployment across the nation’s vital systems.

title: To direct the Director of National Intelligence to submit to Congress a report on the use of artificial intelligence systems to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978.
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: Congress has asked the Director of National Intelligence to prepare a report detailing how artificial‑intelligence systems are used to gather, analyze, query, and share information under Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act. The report is intended to help Congress understand the role and implications of AI in these surveillance programs.

title: To require the Secretary of Homeland Security to carry out prize competitions to advance the science of interpretability and to develop adversarial robustness with respect to artificial intelligence products, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: This policy requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to run prize competitions that encourage research into making AI systems more understandable (interpretability) and harder to trick or attack (adversarial robustness). The goal is to strengthen national security by fostering innovations that help AI systems be safer and more transparent.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: This act is designed to protect consumers from misleading AI, requiring companies to be clear about when they’re using AI and how it works. It sets up rules and penalties to stop deceptive AI practices and promote honesty and transparency.

title: A bill to establish the Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This bill proposes creating a new board called the Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations to oversee and investigate issues related to cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. The board would have authority to investigate incidents, recommend policies, and coordinate with other agencies to protect national security and public safety.

title: A bill to establish the Artificial Intelligence Horizon Fund, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The bill proposes creating the Artificial Intelligence Horizon Fund to provide financial resources for AI research, development, and deployment initiatives. It also includes additional provisions and regulatory measures to guide the responsible growth of AI technologies.

title: READ AI Models Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The READ AI Models Act is a legislative proposal that aims to create clear rules for developing, deploying, and governing AI models to ensure they are safe, transparent, and ethically sound. It requires AI developers to perform risk assessments, disclose model details, and allow independent audits so users can trust that AI systems are built and used responsibly.

title: To establish a human-centered Federal framework for artificial intelligence in education and the workforce, promote the ethical and responsible teaching and learning of artificial intelligence, provide for equitable access to artificial intelligence-ready workforce development, safeguard student and worker data privacy, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committees on Science, Space, and Technology, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: This policy seeks to create a federal framework that places people at the center of how artificial intelligence is used in education and the workforce, ensuring that AI is taught and applied responsibly and ethically. It also aims to give everyone equal access to AI-ready training, protect the privacy of students and workers, and address additional related issues.

title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
summary: This act seeks to protect families from the rising energy costs caused by large AI data centers. It proposes measures like subsidies, tax incentives, or regulatory limits to offset the additional power demand these centers place on households, ensuring that families are not burdened by the electricity expenses associated with AI infrastructure.

title: Department of Advanced Technology and Artificial Intelligence Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
summary: The Department of Advanced Technology and Artificial Intelligence Act creates a new federal department that will lead research, development, and deployment of cutting‑edge technologies and AI. It sets out rules for industry, academia, and government to work together responsibly, ensuring innovation follows ethical standards and protects national security.

title: A bill to establish the Department of Artificial Intelligence and to provide for the regulation of advanced artificial intelligence systems, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This bill proposes creating a new federal Department of Artificial Intelligence to oversee AI research and deployment. It also outlines rules for regulating advanced AI systems to ensure safety, ethics, and accountability.

title: A bill to require disclosure of certain information relating to artificial intelligence systems, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The bill requires companies that create or use artificial intelligence systems to publicly disclose detailed information about the system’s design, purpose, and potential risks. This transparency is intended to help regulators and consumers better understand AI technologies and ensure they are used responsibly.

title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026 seeks to guarantee that AI tools used by veterans are developed and applied with strict ethical standards, preventing bias, privacy violations, and other harms. It establishes clear rules for transparency, accountability, and oversight to protect veterans and build trust in AI systems.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act aims to prevent the creation and deployment of AI systems that could operate unpredictably or dangerously. It proposes strict oversight, mandatory safety testing, and penalties for non‑compliance to keep AI technologies aligned with legal and ethical standards.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act aims to ensure that AI systems used in processing veterans' claims are transparent, fair, and accountable. It requires regular audits, clear documentation, and safeguards against bias to protect veterans’ interests.

title: Covered AI Prohibition Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The Covered AI Prohibition Act is a legislative proposal that bans the use of artificial intelligence in specific high‑risk or sensitive areas. It requires organizations to avoid deploying AI in these covered contexts and establishes enforcement measures to ensure compliance.

title: Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act establishes standards to ensure that AI systems used by the military are reliable and safe. It requires defense contractors and agencies to report any failures, risks, or incidents related to AI so that accountability and continuous improvement can be maintained.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act requires organizations that build and deploy advanced AI systems to perform detailed security assessments and put safeguards in place to prevent misuse. It also creates a framework for monitoring AI deployments, sharing threat information, and coordinating responses to new risks.

title: Ban AI Denials in Medicare Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Ways and Means, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Ban AI Denials in Medicare Act prohibits Medicare beneficiaries from having their claims denied solely based on automated AI decisions, ensuring that coverage decisions remain subject to human review. This act protects patients’ access to healthcare by preventing the use of AI systems as the sole basis for coverage denials.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act bans the construction and operation of new data centers specifically dedicated to artificial intelligence for a set period. It is intended to curb environmental impact, lower carbon emissions, and encourage more sustainable computing practices.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 aims to curb companies from raising AI service prices to exploit consumers and from manipulating labor markets to suppress wages. It would establish rules and penalties to prevent these practices and promote fair competition in AI-related industries.

title: Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 43 - 0.
summary: The Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026 is a U.S. law aimed at protecting AI developers by making it illegal to copy or use AI models without permission. It establishes penalties and enforcement mechanisms to prevent unauthorized extraction and commercial exploitation of AI technology.

title: Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026 establishes a framework for studying and monitoring the use of artificial intelligence in judicial settings, ensuring that AI systems employed in courts are transparent, reliable, and accountable. It creates a dedicated oversight body tasked with conducting research, issuing guidelines, and reviewing AI tools to safeguard fair and unbiased legal processes.

title: SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026
action: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship.
summary: The SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026 sets rules for how the Small Business Administration can use AI, focusing on transparency and accountability to protect small business owners and their data. It requires regular audits, stakeholder input, and safeguards to prevent bias, misuse, and privacy violations in AI tools used by the agency.

title: American Artificial Intelligence Leadership and Uniformity Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The American Artificial Intelligence Leadership and Uniformity Act aims to establish the United States as a global leader in AI development and ensure consistent standards across the industry. It proposes coordinated research, regulatory oversight, and ethical guidelines to govern the deployment of AI technologies.

title: Federal Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Federal Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Act of 2026 establishes a national framework for evaluating and mitigating the risks associated with artificial intelligence systems. It creates federal oversight, requires organizations to develop and report risk management plans, and empowers agencies to enforce compliance with safety and ethical standards for AI technologies.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 619.
summary: This Act encourages the adoption of AI technologies across financial services, aiming to drive innovation and improve efficiency. It provides regulatory guidance and incentives while addressing risk management, privacy, and ethical considerations.

title: HBCU AI Research Leadership Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The HBCU AI Research Leadership Act seeks to foster advanced AI research and development at Historically Black Colleges and Universities. It provides funding, resources, and partnerships to help HBCUs become leaders in AI innovation and to address workforce diversity.
